title: Tunable Multiband Geometry and Fractional Phases in Higher Vortexable Systems
authors: Xiaohan Wan, Siddhartha Sarkar, Ting Cao, Mark Rudner, Di Xiao, Kai Sun
abstract: Higher vortexability is often viewed as a route to topological flat bands with higher-Landau-level-like quantum geometry. Here we emphasize a complementary perspective: it provides a tunable multiband structure in which wave function geometry can be varied continuously while the band dispersion, degeneracy, and topology remain fixed. We perform systematic exact-diagonalization studies of many-body phases in fractionally filled higher vortexable moiré systems, retaining the full flat-band Hilbert space rather than projecting onto a single band. The multiband treatment reveals a cascade of Abelian and non-Abelian phases at zero magnetic field, including integer and fractional exciton insulators, Abelian fractional Chern insulators, Moore-Read and Read-Rezayi states. At fixed filling, different phases are connected through transitions or crossovers driven solely by changes in wave function geometry, highlighting quantum geometry itself as a direct tuning parameter between competing topological states. At fillings associated with Moore-Read and Read-Rezayi states, our calculations show that interband mixing shifts the optimal quantum geometry regime without suppressing non-Abelian topological order under screened Coulomb interaction. Our results establish higher vortexable moiré bands as a tunable platform for exploring geometry-driven multiband topological phases at zero magnetic field.
summary: This work develops the theory of higher vortexable moiré systems, treating them as multiband platforms rather than single-band models. By systematically varying the wave function geometry via interlayer coupling, the authors demonstrate a continuous tuning pathway between numerous correlated topological phases at zero magnetic field. This establishes quantum geometry as a fundamental control parameter for realizing exotic fractional states.
main_problem: To explore tunable multiband geometry and fractional phases in higher vortexable systems, moving beyond the single-band approximation common in previous studies.
main_result: The full multiband treatment reveals a cascade of topological phases connected by transitions driven solely by changes in quantum geometry at zero magnetic field.
method: Systematic exact-diagonalization studies were performed on many-body phases, retaining the full flat-band Hilbert space rather than projecting onto a single band.
model_or_system: The system utilizes higher vortexable moiré systems, which are generalized lattice structures supporting multiple degenerate flat bands. The physics is governed by coupling between layers/bands via an operator D, allowing for continuous tuning of the wave function geometry.

important_parameters: The interlayer hybridization strength, parameterized by an angle $	heta$, acts as the primary tuning parameter for quantum geometry.
main_assumptions: Previous studies often focused on single-band projections, which is insufficient because interband mixing and residual interactions are crucial for stabilizing non-Abelian order.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the evolution of geometric quantities (like the ratio between quantum metric trace and Berry curvature) as a function of $	heta$, and phase diagrams mapping out various Abelian and non-Abelian fractional states across different fillings.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical framework using higher vortexability to define tunable multiband structures. It then performs systematic ED calculations, showing how varying the geometry parameter ($	heta$) drives transitions between distinct topological phases (e.g., Halperin vs. Laughlin/MR states).
why_interesting: The concept of quantum geometry itself being a direct tuning knob for accessing different correlated topological states is highly relevant to understanding tunable Hamiltonians in AMO systems, such as those realized with optical lattices or superconducting circuits.
